name: basic-auth-fallback
description:
A cluster that rejects per-request HTTP Basic auth with a 401. Whether HyperCore v1 accepts Basic on every route is unverified against a real cluster -- Scale's own tooling authenticates via POST /rest/v1/login and a session cookie -- so the script keeps Basic as the first attempt and falls back to the login session once when Basic gets a 401. The first Cluster call answers 401, the login succeeds, the Cluster call is retried, and the rest of the walk proceeds; a run without the fallback imports nothing, ever, on such a cluster.

The network device row also carries a link-local 169.254 guest address alongside the real one, pinning that guest-reported IP lists are filtered through routable_ips before they become an interface -- an unfiltered link-local address cross-correlates unrelated VMs (and the no_loopback_interfaces invariant would fail).

namespaced_ids is skipped because the foreign id is the bare HC3 VirDomain UUID with no cluster or appliance scope, as in the other scenarios. Pre-existing, not introduced here.

log_contains: scale-computing: Basic auth was rejected; continuing with a /rest/v1/login session
